It helps users explore environmental changes, analyze historical trends, and understand their significance using Earth science data. Its core analysis uses NASA POWER Daily data from 1991 to 2024 across six locations in Bangladesh. Through four connected workspaces, Explore Earth, Research Workspace, Student Lab, and Claim Court, users can visualize environmental trends, perform statistical analysis using Mann Kendall and Theil Sen methods, investigate real NASA data through guided learning, and evaluate environmental claims using evidence. Features like the Trend Divergence Detector and Data Passport connect data exploration with scientific evidence, making Earth science more accessible to students, researchers, and the public.
details:
BHUSANKET: Earth Systems Discovery & Evidence Lab

BhuSanket is a Bangladesh-first, globally adaptable Earth systems discovery and evidence platform developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026: "Be an Earth System Trend Detective!" It helps students, researchers, and curious citizens explore environmental changes, investigate long-term trends, and understand what the data actually reveals.

HOW IT WORKS

BhuSanket brings environmental data exploration, scientific analysis, and interactive learning together in one platform. Its core analysis uses NASA POWER Daily historical data (1991–2024) across six locations in Bangladesh, covering five environmental parameters. Users can select a location, choose an environmental variable, adjust the time period, and explore changes through interactive maps and time-series visualizations.

The Research Workspace applies the Mann–Kendall test to assess trend significance and the Theil–Sen estimator to measure the rate of change. Users can examine trend direction, slope, p-values, and confidence intervals. The Analysis-Window Slider allows users to investigate different time periods, while the Trend Divergence Detector compares patterns across regions to reveal where environmental changes agree or differ.

OUR FOUR WORKSPACES

  1. Explore Earth: An interactive geographical workspace where users explore environmental patterns across Bangladesh's districts through maps, selected variables, and historical trends.
  2. Research Workspace: A scientific investigation environment featuring statistical trend analysis, regional comparisons, and evidence-based results.
  3. Student Lab: A guided learning environment with missions, lessons, quizzes, worksheets, and hands-on NASA data investigations. It encourages students to develop hypotheses, explore real environmental datasets, and discover patterns themselves.
  4. Claim Court: An interactive evidence-verification experience where users examine environmental claims, review supporting and counter-evidence, assess confidence, and reach evidence-based verdicts.

SIGNATURE INNOVATIONS

BhuSanket goes beyond conventional climate dashboards through several connected features. The NASA Mission-to-Evidence Trail connects data sources to variables, locations, analysis, and results. The Data Passport documents the origin and methodology behind each finding. The Climate Claim Checker, Earth Impact Lens, and Ask BhuSanket further support environmental understanding, evidence exploration, and guided discovery.

NASA DATA AND RESOURCES

Our core working analysis uses NASA POWER Daily. Our broader data catalogue and exploration resources include GPM IMERG precipitation estimates, MODIS land-surface temperature and vegetation products, NASA GIBS Earth imagery, Blue Marble geographic context, and Giovanni for NASA data exploration and visualization. These resources provide pathways for expanding the platform across additional Earth-system variables and datasets.

TECHNOLOGY USED

The platform is developed using Next.js, React, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS for the frontend, with Python and FastAPI powering the backend. NumPy, Pandas, and SciPy support data processing and statistical analysis, while MapLibre and Leaflet support geographical visualization.

IMPACT AND FUTURE VISION

BhuSanket aims to make Earth science more accessible, understandable, and evidence-driven. It connects classroom learning with real scientific investigation, gives researchers a structured environment for exploring environmental trends, and helps communities better understand changes affecting their surroundings.

Our next steps include expanding geographical coverage beyond Bangladesh, integrating additional NASA Earth-observation datasets into the analysis workflow, improving learning experiences, and strengthening evidence-based environmental discovery.

BhuSanket is more than a climate dashboard. It is a connected environment where people can explore Earth, test trends, question claims, and discover the evidence behind environmental change.

Developed by Team Synastra, Bangladesh.
